title: The tautological right slice cone compares straightening with a representable
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, Kan complexes, internal functor simplicial sets and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in universes containing all displayed constructions. Use concrete slices and right-pinched mapping spaces of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], the cone functor $T_K$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], and $J^n,Q^n,|{-}|_Q,\theta$ of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. Let $C,K$ be small quasicategories, $c\in C_0$ and $v:K\to C$. Set $E=K\times_C C_{/c}$ and let $q:E\to K$ be projection. Put $A=\mathfrak C[K]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $R(k)=\mathfrak C[C](v(k),c)$, with action by precomposition with $\mathfrak C[v]$. The tautological cone $\varepsilon:E\star\Delta^0\to C$, sending the new vertex to $c$ and the simplex $(\sigma:\Delta^n\to K,\tau:\Delta^{n+1}\to C)$ of $E$ to its displayed cone $\tau$, induces an enriched natural transformation
$$\psi:T_K(E)\longrightarrow R.$$
On a mixed simplex with a repeated final cone vertex, $\varepsilon$ uses $\tau$ after collapse of that repeated block. Every component $\psi_k$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. More precisely, the fibre inclusion gives a canonical weak homotopy equivalence $|E_k|_Q\to T_K(E)(k)$, and its composite with $\psi_k$ is exactly $\theta_{C,v(k),c}$ under $E_k=\operatorname{Map}^R_C(v(k),c)$. The equality is an equality of simplicial maps: on the $Q^n$ summand indexed by $e\in(E_k)_n$ it is induced by the enriched realization of the map $J^n\to C$ given by $e$. These maps are natural in the displayed inputs and all simplex operators. Composing $\psi$ with the realization/singular units gives an objectwise weak equivalence $T_K(E)\to H$, where $H(k)=\operatorname{Sing}|R(k)|$ has its enriched precomposition action from [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces].

source.place: Returned Step 14, tautological cone and pinched-resolution comparison; HTT 2.2.2.7, 2.2.3.15, 2.2.4.1 Argument extracted from the returned proof; HTT supplies the background constructions, not a verbatim assertion of this formulated lemma. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical comparison.

proof.text: Use the ordered cone formula for $T_K$: $T_K(E)(k)=M_q(k,v)$ with $M_q=\mathfrak C[E\star\Delta^0]\amalg_{\mathfrak C[E]}\mathfrak C[K]$. The restriction of $\varepsilon$ to $E\subseteq E\star\Delta^0$ is $v\circ q$: for a simplex $(\sigma,\tau)$ of $E=K\times_C C_{/c}$ the restriction of $\tau$ to the initial face $\Delta^n$ is $v\sigma$ by the definition of the fibre product, and $\varepsilon$ is a simplicial map because the ordered-concatenation operators on mixed simplices (with the repeated final cone vertex collapsed) are precomposition of $\tau$ with the corresponding monotone maps. Hence $\mathfrak C[\varepsilon]$ and $\mathfrak C[v]$ agree on $\mathfrak C[E]$ and induce a simplicial functor $M_q\to\mathfrak C[C]$ sending $k\mapsto v(k)$ and the new cone vertex to $c$. Its maps on mapping simplicial sets into the cone vertex are $\psi_k:T_K(E)(k)=M_q(k,v)\to\mathfrak C[C](v(k),c)=R(k)$. Because the functor restricts to $\mathfrak C[v]$ on $\mathfrak C[K]$, these maps are compatible with precomposition in $\mathfrak C[K]$ on the source and with precomposition by $\mathfrak C[v]$ on the target, so they assemble to an enriched natural transformation $\psi:T_K(E)\to R$. If the final cone vertex is repeated, the ordered-cone operators first collapse that repeated block; applying $\tau$ after this collapse is exactly the compatible formula.

source.place: HTT 2.2.2.7 and 2.2.3.15; returned Step 14 cone formula

proof.text: For a vertex $k$, the projection $q:E\to K$ is a right fibration: it is the pullback along $v$ of the right fibration $C_{/c}\to C$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and the right lifting property against $\Lambda^n_i\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is stable under pullback. Its fibre is $E_k=\{k\}\times_KE=\{v(k)\}\times_CC_{/c}=\operatorname{Map}^R_C(v(k),c)$ by the same node. The cone functor $T_K$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] and $\operatorname{St}_K$ of [lem-coef-right-straightening-fiber-comparison] are given by the same formula $M_q(k,v)$ (both joins are the ordered concatenation with $\Delta^0$ and both $\mathfrak C$ are the subset-poset rigidification), so $T_K(E)=\operatorname{St}_K(E)$. Over a point, $\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^0}(-)(*)$ is $|{-}|_Q$ (HTT p.~76, before 2.2.2.6): both functors preserve small colimits ($\operatorname{St}$ by [lem-coef-right-straightening-fiber-comparison], $|{-}|_Q$ as the left adjoint of $\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ in [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]); $\mathfrak C$ is the left adjoint of the coherent nerve [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] and so preserves the pushout $J^n=\Delta^{n+1}\amalg_{\Delta^n}\{x\}$, whence $\operatorname{St}_{\Delta^0}(\Delta^n)(*)=\mathfrak C[J^n](x,y)=Q^n$; and for monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ the induced map of pushouts restricts to $\Delta(\alpha)$ on the initial face and fixes the cone vertex, so it is $Q(\alpha)$. Writing a simplicial set as the colimit of its simplices gives the natural identification. Therefore the right-straightening fibre comparison, applied to the right fibration $q$ and the vertex $k$, gives a canonical weak equivalence $i_k:|E_k|_Q\to T_K(E)(k)$, induced by the fibre inclusion. On the $Q^n$ summand indexed by $e\in(E_k)_n$, i.e. $e:J^n\to C$ via its cone component, the composite $\psi_ki_k$ is $\mathfrak C$ applied to $J^n\to E_k\star\Delta^0\amalg_{E_k}\{k\}\to C$, which is $e$; so it is the mapping-set map of $\mathfrak C[J^n]\to\mathfrak C[C]$ induced by $e$. By the pinched-rigidification comparison this is precisely $\theta_{C,v(k),c}$, in every simplicial degree and with all operators.

source.place: HTT p. 76 (St over a point is ||_{Q^•}, J^n, Q^n) and HTT 2.2.4.1 proof (f = f''∘f'); returned Step 14 pinched-resolution comparison

proof.text: Both $i_k$ and $\theta_{C,v(k),c}=\psi_k i_k$ are weak homotopy equivalences. The two-out-of-three property therefore makes every component $\psi_k$ a weak homotopy equivalence.

Let $u_k:R(k)\to\operatorname{Sing}|R(k)|$ be the characteristic realization/singular unit. The concrete space-valued representable construction identifies $H(k)$ with $\operatorname{Sing}|R(k)|$ and gives it the enriched precomposition action. The realization/singular-unit theorem says $u_k$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every simplicial set $R(k)$. Hence $u_k\psi_k:T_K(E)(k)\to H(k)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by closure under composition, so these maps form an objectwise weak equivalence $T_K(E)\to H$.

All constructions above are functorial in $C,K,c,v$: pullback fibres, the cone map $\varepsilon$, enriched precomposition, and the maps on $Q^n$ commute with the corresponding maps of inputs. The pinched-rigidification statement supplies naturality in the displayed inputs and all simplex operators, while the cone and space-valued representable constructions supply the same precomposition actions. Thus the equality $\psi_k i_k=\theta_{C,v(k),c}$ and the objectwise weak equivalence are natural for the displayed inputs and every face and degeneracy.
